lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Housing blocks laid out in a grid below, lit to exactly the level the Steward has decided a night requires. Past them, the dark where the coast drops away to the water.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Forty thousand people on this entire coast. The archive says nine million lived here once, before the water came up, and it does not say where they went — it simply counts fewer of them each quarter until the number stops moving.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I have read that figure a hundred times and I have never once been able to make it feel like anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The corridor lights are on now. All of them, the whole length. And there is a shape at the far end of the glass that is not on this side of it.
